answer: Intergenerational mentoring resists sybils by binding each agent identity to a mentor lineage whose verified knowledge-transfer history forms a knoll of attested reputation that new identities cannot cheaply clone. As the tide of new registrations rises, elders must co-sign protégé credentials on a public terrace of apprenticeship records, forcing every sybil to recruit. Colluding clusters incur an exponential slashing penalty bounded by O(Delta * S).
